CausalChain: Chronic liver injury and inflammation lead to overexpression of oncogenes such as AEG‐1 and recruitment of regulatory T cells → Elevated AEG‐1 promotes tumor proliferation and further reinforces an immunosuppressive microenvironment → Nanoparticle delivery systems enable targeted CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated knockout of AEG‐1 in HCC cells, reducing its oncogenic influence → Concurrent PD‐1 blockade reverses T cell exhaustion and diminishes Treg‐mediated suppression → The combined reduction in tumor intrinsic drive and enhanced cytotoxic T cell activity results in synergistic, durable tumor regression.
Hypothesis: Nanoparticle‐mediated CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of AEG‐1 combined with PD‐1 checkpoint inhibition will synergistically re‐program the immunosuppressive microenvironment of HCC, leading to enhanced cytotoxic T cell activity and sustained tumor regression.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a difficult-to-treat cancer due to its complex microenvironment, frequent resistance to conventional therapies, and a highly immunosuppressive milieu. Recent advances in gene therapy, including CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated genome editing, nanoparticle‐delivered siRNAs, and immune checkpoint inhibitors, suggest that targeting both oncogenic drivers and the immune evasion mechanisms may result in synergistic antitumor effects. Here, we propose a dual-targeted therapeutic strategy that simultaneously disrupts oncogenic signaling and reduces immunosuppression to re‐program the tumor microenvironment. Specifically, we hypothesize that nanoparticle‐facilitated CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of the oncogene AEG‐1 in HCC cells, in combination with immune checkpoint blockade using PD‐1 inhibitors, can reinvigorate cytotoxic T cell responses, overcome tumor immune tolerance, and ultimately lead to durable tumor regression. This combinatorial approach may provide a new avenue for personalized and effective HCC therapy.
